facts.text: Far Ultraviolet Camera/Spectrograph was deployed at Descartes Highlands during Apollo 16 in 1972.

The first telescope operated from another world. George Carruthers' UV camera photographed Earth's geocorona, the Milky Way, the Large Magellanic Cloud, and nebulae — all in wavelengths blocked by Earth's atmosphere.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.

Captured the first astronomical photographs from another world, imaging Earth's hydrogen geocorona, the Large Magellanic Cloud, and nebulae in far-ultraviolet wavelengths that cannot penetrate Earth's atmosphere.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Descartes Highlands.
Remains at Descartes; it was designed by Dr. George Carruthers of the Naval Research Laboratory, who was later inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame for this work.
